stem: What is the surgical principle behind the Soave procedure for Hirschsprung's disease?

options.text: A straight end-to-end anastomosis after full resection
A pull-through of normal colon through an aganglionic muscular cuff
Creating a side-to-side anastomosis in the retrorectal plane
Total abdominal colectomy with an ileostomy

explanation: The Soave procedure leaves the muscular wall of the rectum intact to protect pelvic nerves while pulling normal bowel through it.
rationale: Consider the technique that focuses on preserving the pelvic nerves by working within a 'cuff' of the rectum.

optionExplanations.A: A straight end-to-end anastomosis is the principle behind the Swenson procedure, not the Soave.
optionExplanations.B: The Soave procedure leaves the muscular wall of the rectum intact to protect pelvic nerves while pulling normal bowel through it.
optionExplanations.C: This describes the Duhamel procedure, which leaves an aganglionic anterior wall and creates a new posterior passage.
optionExplanations.D: While occasionally necessary for total colonic aganglionosis, this is not the defining principle of the Soave procedure.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: A pull-through of normal colon through an aganglionic muscular cuff
